# Full-Stack Engineer (TypeScript / React) – Patient Experience

**Company:** Verdane Care (FICTIONAL)
**Location:** Graz, Austria (hybrid) or fully remote within Austria, Germany, Croatia or Slovenia
**Employment:** Full-time, permanent (or B2B contract in Croatia on request)
**Team:** Patient Experience squad (4 engineers, 1 designer, 1 product manager)

## About the role

Verdane Care makes appointment-booking and follow-up software for private clinics and physiotherapy practices. Patients use our web app and mobile web experience to book visits, fill in intake forms, receive reminders and view exercise plans.

As a Full-Stack Engineer you will build and improve those patient-facing features end to end – from React components and accessibility to the Node.js APIs and the database behind them. You will work in a small squad with a designer and a product manager, and you will ship to production several times a week.

## What you will do

- Build new patient-facing features in React and TypeScript, with a strong focus on accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA) and performance on low-end phones
- Implement Node.js (NestJS) APIs and PostgreSQL schemas to support those features
- Integrate with third-party systems such as clinic calendars, SMS providers and payment gateways
- Write unit, integration and end-to-end tests (Jest, Playwright) and keep the build green
- Take part in design reviews, usability sessions and sprint planning
- Handle personal health data responsibly: follow our GDPR and data-minimisation guidelines, support audit requests from clinic customers
- Mentor interns or junior colleagues when the opportunity arises

## What you bring

**Must have**
- 2+ years of professional experience building web applications with React and TypeScript
- Experience writing backend services in Node.js (Express, NestJS or similar) and working with SQL databases
- Understanding of semantic HTML, responsive layouts and web accessibility basics
- Experience with automated testing (unit and end-to-end) and Git-based workflows
- Awareness of web security fundamentals (authentication, OWASP Top 10) and willingness to learn the privacy requirements of health data
- Fluent English; German or Croatian is helpful for customer-facing conversations

**Nice to have**
- Experience with Next.js or other server-side rendering frameworks
- Experience in healthcare, wellness or other regulated environments
- Familiarity with AWS or a similar cloud, and with Docker
- Experience with design systems and Storybook
- Experience with analytics and A/B testing

## What we offer

- Salary range EUR 54,000 – 70,000 gross per year depending on experience (Austrian collective agreement minimum applies)
- 25 days of holiday plus the Austrian public holidays, 5 additional well-being days and a EUR 1,200 yearly education budget
- Flexible hours, a home-office stipend and a yearly team retreat
- A friendly, low-ego team that cares about the people who use our software

## How to apply

Send your CV. A short cover letter and a link to something you have built (a portfolio, a GitHub project or a live site) are welcome but optional. We reply within ten working days.

Verdane Care is committed to a diverse and inclusive workplace and welcomes applications from career changers and people returning to work.

1. In the Professional Summary, retain the existing React/TypeScript and Node.js/PostgreSQL positioning but make the strongest role-relevant evidence more compact and prominent. For example, replace the final sentence with: "Recent fintech work includes BankID identity verification, secure ID-document upload, and an incremental Express-to-NestJS backend migration, with measurable onboarding conversion improvement from 61% to 74%." This improves relevance without adding unsupported claims.
2. In the Full-Stack Developer section under Älvgrind Fintech AB, remove the cross-reference wording "see Selected Projects for details" from the BankID and secure-upload bullets. Replace each with a self-contained achievement bullet, for example: "Built a BankID identity-verification step for onboarding with QR-code and same-device flows; A/B testing increased onboarding conversion from 61% to 74%." and "Implemented secure ID-document uploads using S3 presigned URLs, ClamAV scanning in Lambda, SQS status handling, and PostgreSQL." This makes the experience section stronger when parsed independently by an ATS or AI screener.
3. In the Core Skills section, change the label "Databases and ORM" to "Databases, SQL and ORM" because the job explicitly requests SQL database experience. Keep the listed technologies truthful, for example: "PostgreSQL; TypeORM; Prisma." Do not claim generic SQL proficiency beyond what the PostgreSQL work supports.
4. In the Full-Stack Developer section, make the security-relevant work more explicit without claiming OWASP expertise. Change the secure-upload wording to include the existing evidence of "presigned URLs," "ClamAV virus scanning," and "scan-status handling." This will better connect the documented work to the job's web-security and sensitive-data responsibilities.
5. In the Languages section, change "English" to "English — professional working proficiency" only if that accurately reflects the candidate's actual proficiency. The supplied English-language application demonstrates English use, but it does not independently verify fluency; do not use "fluent" unless accurate.

MINOR ATS / PRESENTATION ENHANCEMENTS
6. In the Professional Experience section, standardize the Nordkust Media entry to match the other entries: "Developer | Nordkust Media | 2014–2018." The current company name and dates are split across separate lines, which is still readable but less consistent for parsing.
7. In the Core Skills section, change "Cloud and messaging" to "Cloud, Storage and Messaging" because the listed AWS services include ECS, S3, Lambda, and SQS. This gives the section a more precise searchable label without adding new skills.
8. In the Home Assistant Integrations project, retain the GitHub and approximately 40-stars evidence, but include the actual GitHub URL if the candidate wants the CV to provide a verifiable project link. Do not invent or imply a URL that was not supplied.

cover_letter_history.content:
Dear Verdane Care team,

I’m applying for the Full-Stack Engineer role on the Patient Experience squad. I’m a full-stack developer with 12 years of professional experience, strongest in React and TypeScript, and with hands-on experience building Node.js services and working with PostgreSQL. Verdane Care’s focus on patient-facing tools, accessible design and privacy by default makes this role especially compelling.

In my current role at Älvgrind Fintech, I build onboarding features using React, TypeScript, NestJS and PostgreSQL. I built a BankID identity-verification flow that was A/B tested before rollout; onboarding conversion increased from 61% to 74%. I also implemented a secure ID-document upload flow using S3 presigned URLs, virus scanning in Lambda and scan-status handling through SQS. These projects have given me practical experience building end-to-end features where usability and careful handling of sensitive information matter.

I’ve also contributed to an incremental migration of an onboarding backend from Express to NestJS, and maintained an Apollo Server BFF. Earlier, as project tech lead in a two-developer team, I built most of a React Native ferry-ticket app, which now has around 50,000 downloads. I’d be glad to bring this mix of frontend strength, backend delivery and hands-on product experience to Verdane Care’s patient-facing work.

Thank you for considering my application. I’d welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience could contribute to the Patient Experience squad.

Best regards,
Oskar

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is concise, professional, well structured, and tailored to Verdane Care’s Patient Experience role. It presents strong evidence through concrete outcomes, including the 61% to 74% onboarding conversion increase and the approximately 50,000 mobile-app downloads. The examples also demonstrate end-to-end delivery, frontend strength, backend experience, and responsible handling of sensitive information. The main weakness is completeness: several requirements that the candidate may be able to support are not surfaced, particularly security fundamentals, accessibility, testing, Git workflows, and willingness to learn health-data privacy requirements. These omissions limit the letter’s persuasive value, although they do not indicate that the candidate lacks those capabilities.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter is ATS-friendly: it uses standard headings-free prose, conventional punctuation, readable paragraphs, and relevant exact terms such as React, TypeScript, Node.js, NestJS, PostgreSQL, AWS, S3, Lambda, SQS, Express, and A/B tested. There are no tables, graphics, unusual symbols, or formatting elements likely to impair parsing. AI screening probability is good when the associated CV is considered because the CV contains the strongest technical keyword coverage. For the cover letter alone, screening coverage is moderate rather than excellent because it does not explicitly include terms from the advertisement such as accessibility, automated testing, Git-based workflows, authentication, or privacy requirements.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: Alignment is strong for the core full-stack stack: the document clearly shows substantially more than two years of React and TypeScript experience, Node.js backend work, SQL/PostgreSQL, AWS familiarity, and analytics/A/B testing. The identity-verification and secure-document-upload examples are relevant to Verdane Care’s privacy-by-default focus, although the letter appropriately does not claim healthcare experience. The ferry-ticket application supports product ownership, mobile usability, and technical leadership. The document does not show semantic HTML, responsive layouts, web accessibility, automated unit/integration/end-to-end testing, Git workflows, OWASP Top 10 awareness, German or Croatian, Next.js/server-side rendering, Docker, design systems, or Storybook. The candidate material also does not establish healthcare experience or explicit willingness to learn health-data privacy requirements. These are candidate-evidence gaps or unsupported areas, not defects that should be invented through rewriting.
